Procurement asked me to surface a short list of tradeoffs and expected timelines for each approach so we can decide which lane to pursue.

- How long does a marketplace listing take vs a private offer from Redwood?

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Lauren (channel & billing) to confirm partner/co-sell considerations. Quick summary up front: both lanes are viable; the decision usually rests on (1) how quickly you need to start, (2) whether you require PO/invoice terms and custom SKUs, and (3) whether you want the co-sell incentives tied to a marketplace listing.

Marketplace listing (fast path):
- Typical timing: if you buy "off-the-shelf" from our existing marketplace listing, procurement can complete in 2–5 business days if Clearwave uses the AWS account billing flow and no contract redlines are required.
- Pros: fastest billing integration, immediate use of cloud credits and consolidated billing, marketplace incentives may reduce net cost.
- Cons: less flexibility on custom SKUs, PO-based billing is often more complex (some customers still route through their cloud billing).

Private Offer / Direct invoice (controlled path):
- Typical timing: Private Offer setup + legal + PO turnaround generally 7–15 business days (depends on legal review & PO cadence). If you need custom SKUs or commit discounts, this is the route.
- Pros: supports PO-to-invoice flow, custom SKUs/pricing, can include MSA addendum and explicit SLA terms; better for regulated procurement.
- Cons: slightly longer procurement lead time; co-sell incentives depend on marketplace listing status (we can often register co-sell separately).

Next steps I recommend:
1) If you need to start the pilot by mid-May: go marketplace for initial consumption and use that time to process a private offer in parallel.
2) If PO/invoicing is required immediately: start the private offer now; we can speed legal review with a short MSA addendum.

I'll attach a PO template and our Private Offer checklist to help procurement scope timelines. Lauren — can you add guidance on co-sell registration and incentive timing?

Attachments: Clearwave_PO_Template.pdf, Redwood_Private_Offer_Checklist.xlsx

Best,

Hi Olivia — quick color on co-sell and incentives from the channel side. (Looping in Karthik for technical SKU mapping & partner ops.)

Co-sell / marketplace notes:
- If Clearwave buys through the AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace, the transaction is eligible for standard marketplace co-sell programs (timing: registration of the opportunity in partner portal typically within 2–4 business days after purchase record is available). That means incentive payouts are generally faster.
- For private offers, we can still register the deal for co-sell credit, but it requires manual registration and approval which can add 5–10 business days. We typically see customers get equivalent net economics but with more administrative steps.
- Support & SLA: identical across lanes once the customer account is onboarded to Redwood Dedicated/Hosted — the difference is billing flow only. Data residency options are the same for both routes if you require specific region constraints; that is handled at onboarding.

Recommendation: If procurement can accept a short-term marketplace invoice for the pilot, do that for speed and early co-sell eligibility. Start the private offer in parallel if you need PO invoicing and commit pricing. We'll prioritize the private-offer paperwork so you have both options within the next 2 weeks.

I'll follow up with Karthik to map the exact SKU/consumption expectations for the pilot so finance can estimate spend.

Thanks,
